samples.summary: Remote-change clear drops the image selection but leaves an in-flight resize drag armed, violating the invariant editor.ts documents for exactly this case
samples.evidence: The new `editor.clearImageSelection()` in `store.onRemoteChange` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:392) resolves to `clearImageSelectionForMutation` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1295-1299), which only nulls `selectedImage` and renders — it never calls `abortImageResizeDrag()`. But `abortImageResizeDrag`'s own contract at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2578-2591 states: "every path that clears the image selection because the offsets moved under it has to drop the drag too, or the next `mouseup` commits the drag's size onto whatever inline now sits at that coordinate." The three in-module direct-assignment paths (`undoFn` 2111-2115, `redoFn` 2150-2151, `resetAfterDocumentReplace` 3953-3958) all honour that; this new out-of-module caller does not. A remote peer editing while a local user holds a resize handle is exactly the concurrent case the invariant guards: `imageResizeDrag` still holds the stale `(blockId, offset)` captured at mousedown, `render()` keeps painting `imageResizeDrag.previewRect` even with `selectedImage === null` (editor.ts:1852-1853), and `handleImageResizeMouseUp` (editor.ts:2527-2572) then commits `width/height` onto whatever image inline happens to sit at that offset after the peer's edit — the `findImageAtOffset` guard at 2555 only catches the case where no image is there at all, not the case where a *different* image slid into the slot. Fix most likely belongs on the new code path in editor.ts (have `clearImageSelectionForMutation` also call `abortImageResizeDrag()`), not in docs-view.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out. docs-view.tsx:392 does call editor.clearImageSelection() in store.onRemoteChange; the export at editor.ts:3845 resolves to clearImageSelectionForMutation (editor.ts:1295-1299), which only nulls selectedImage and renders and never calls abortImageResizeDrag(). The invariant is documented verbatim at editor.ts:2578-2591 ("every path that clears the image selection because the offsets moved under it has to drop the drag too"), and all three in-module direct-assignment paths honour it (undoFn 2111-2115, redoFn 2150-2151, resetAfterDocumentReplace 3954-3958). The bypass is reachable: the mouseup/mousemove listeners are installed on `document` at editor.ts:2654-2655 and survive the clear; handleImageResizeMouseUp (2527-2576) guards only for a missing block/absent image at 2554-2555, so a different image that slid into (blockId, offset) after the peer edit receives the drag's width/height via applyInlineStyle at 2566-2572. render() at 1852-1858 keys the overlay off imageResizeDrag alone, so the preview keeps painting with selectedImage === null. No deferral exists on the remote path — yorkie-doc-store.ts:579 fires onRemoteChange unconditionally — and the nearest test (copy-integrity.test.ts:1190-1204) only asserts the selection is nulled, never arming a drag. This is a new out-of-module caller violating an invariant the owning module documents, with the broken site outside the diff: in-lane for blast-radius and major by impact (wrong-result mutation onto an unrelated image).

finding.summary: Remote-change path never clears the image selection, so the new "any offset-shifting mutation clears it" invariant is bypassed by every collaborator edit
finding.evidence: The diff establishes the rule that any mutation shifting offsets must call `clearImageSelectionForMutation()` (editor.ts:1288 and its ~15 call sites). The remote path is the one mutation source that never does: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:378-393` (`store.onRemoteChange`) calls `editor.getDoc().refresh()`, `editor.restoreLocalCursor(...)`, `editor.validateCursorPosition()` and `editor.render()` — none of which touches `selectedImage` (`restoreLocalCursor` at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3917-3931 only moves the cursor and sets the selection range; `validateCursorPosition` at editor.ts:979-987 likewise). A peer inserting or deleting text before the selected image shifts the `(blockId, offset)` coordinate the selection is expressed in. The hardening added in this diff only protects against the block/inline being *gone*: `deleteSelectedImageInline` and `imageSelectionProvider` re-validate with `findImageAtOffset`, which merely asserts that *some* image sits at that offset — so where a remote edit slides a different image onto the slot (exactly the `blockWithTwoImages` scenario the new tests use for local mutations), Cmd/Ctrl+X or Delete removes/copies the wrong image, and the overlay is painted around it beforehand. Fix belongs at the docs-view remote handler (call `editor.clearImageSelection()` there, the same seam the find bar was given at docs-find-bar.tsx:124) or inside `restoreLocalCursor`.

verdict.reason: The remote-change path already performs the clear the finding says is missing. packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:392 calls editor.clearImageSelection() as the first statement of store.onRemoteChange, before getDoc().refresh() (line 393) and restoreLocalCursor() (line 394), with a comment stating precisely the invariant in question. packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3845 exports clearImageSelection as clearImageSelectionForMutation, the same helper defined at editor.ts:1295-1299 that the ~15 local mutation sites call, so the remote handler is funnelled through the identical guard. editor.ts:1284-1293 explicitly enumerates the two out-of-module mutation sources (find bar and store.onRemoteChange) that must self-clear, and both are wired. The proposed fix ("call editor.clearImageSelection() there") is already present at the exact file the finding names.
